title: Cultoor
description: Ten mini stories about experiencing culture on the Isle of Man and in Ireland: an art gallery, the Manx Museum, a science evening, a poetry night, Gaelic football, a TV sitcom, a Manx class, a food festival, a holy well and a Viking ship.

lessons.title: Yn galleree noa
lessons.summary: Moira Quarrie, a painter, visits a new art gallery in Douglas with her husband Huw: a beautiful painting of a deer in the rays of the sun, an empty wall with a ladder and dust beside it, a new picture brought from a van over there, and a great feeling of pleasure.
lessons.text:
Va galleree noa foshlit ayns Doolish 'sy vee shoh. Ta Moira Quarrie ny peinteyr, as v'ee laccal y galleree noa y akin. Laa Jeheiney, hie ee dys y galleree marish e sheshey Huw.

Va'n galleree ayns shenn thie mooar faggys da'n traie. Va ny boallaghyn bane, as va soilshey mie ayns ny shamyryn. Ayns y chied shamyr, va jallooyn jeh'n ellan: slieau, glion as traie. “Ta ny jallooyn shoh aalin,” dooyrt Huw.

Ayns y nah shamyr, honnick Moira jalloo mooar jeh feeaih. Va'n feeaih shassoo ayns keyll, as va scellyn y ghrian çheet sheese trooid ny biljyn er e chione. Va ennaght feer vie ec Moira tra honnick ee yn jalloo. “Shoh yn jalloo s'aalin ayns y galleree,” dooyrt ee. “Jeeagh er ny scellyn sollys er y feeaih!” Va'n jalloo peintit ec peinteyr aeg veih Rhumsaa. Va'n peinteyr cliaghtey shooyl 'sy cheyll dy akin ny feeaih.

Ayns y trass shamyr, va boalley follym. Cha row jalloo erbee er. Va aarey ec cass y voalley, as va joan er y laare. “Cre'n fa ta'n boalley shoh follym?” dooyrt Moira rish dooinney aeg va gobbraghey ayns y galleree.

“Ta jalloo noa çheet jiu,” dooyrt eh. “T'eh ayns y van hoal.” Honnick ad van gorrym hoal er y straid. “Ta feme aym yn joan y ghlenney roish my vees y jalloo er y voalley.” Ren eh yn joan y ghlenney, as eisht haink jees dooinney stiagh lesh y jalloo noa.

Hie fer jeu seose yn aarey, as ren ad y jalloo y chroghey er y voalley. Cha row y boalley follym nish. She jalloo jeh'n cheayn v'ayn, as scellyn y ghrian er yn ushtey.

Va taitnys mooar ec Moira ayns y galleree. “S'mie lhiam yn ennaght t'aym ayns shoh,” dooyrt ee rish Huw. “Ta taitnys aym kinjagh ayns jallooyn aalin.” Chionnee Huw lioar veg jeh ny jallooyn er e son.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi hie dys y galleree marish Moira?
Hie e sheshey Huw marish Moira.
Cre va ayns y jalloo mooar 'sy nah shamyr?
Va feeaih ayns keyll ayn, as scellyn y ghrian er.
Cre'n fa va'n boalley follym?
Va jalloo noa çheet, as v'eh ayns y van hoal.
Cre va er y laare?
Va joan er y laare.
Quoi hie seose yn aarey?
Hie dooinney seose yn aarey dy chroghey y jalloo.

lessons.title: Yn ushylagh mooar
lessons.summary: Ffion and her grandfather Gerald Kinnear visit the Manx Museum: the skeleton of a giant deer, a bird with blue feathers, cells with organelles, archaea, a room of animal phyla, a game about metabolism and a model of the human brain.
lessons.text:
Ta Ffion nuy bleeaney d'eash. Laa dy row, hie ee marish e shenn-ayr Gerald Kinnear dys Thie-tashtee Vannin ayns Doolish.

Ayns y chied shamyr, va ushylagh mooar. She ushylagh feeaih v'ayn, feeaih mooar va cummal 'syn ellan roish thousaneyn dy vleeantyn. “Ta'n ushylagh ny s'yrjey na dooinney!” dooyrt Ffion. “Ta,” dooyrt Gerald. “Agh cha nel fynney er ushylagh. Va fynney dhone er y feeaih tra v'eh bio.”

Faggys da'n ushylagh, va ushag ayns kishtey. Va clooie gorrym er yn ushag, as va'n clooie bog as aalin. “Vel clooie er dy chooilley ushag?” dooyrt Ffion. “Ta,” dooyrt Gerald. “As ta fynney er ram beiyn, myr y moddey as y kayt.” “Vel fynney er eeast?” dooyrt Ffion. “Cha nel,” dooyrt Gerald, as ren eh gearey. “Cha nel fynney erbee er eeast.”

Ayns y nah shamyr, va jallooyn mooarey jeh killagyn. Lhaih Gerald yn screeu er y voalley: “Ta killagyn eukaryotagh ec beiyn, lossreeyn as fungyssyn. Ta mynoltyn ayns killag eukaryotagh. Ta dagh mynolt myr shamyr veg, as ta obbyr hene ec dagh mynolt.” Va jalloo elley ayn jeh archaea. “Ta archaea feer veg,” lhaih Gerald, “as cha nel ad eukaryotagh. Ta archaea cummal ayns ushtey feer çheh, raad nagh vel cretooryn elley abyl cummal.”

Ayns y trass shamyr, va ny beiyn ayns possanyn. “Ta phylum myr possan mooar dy veiyn,” dooyrt Gerald. “Ta shin hene ayns yn un phylum as ny eeast as ny ushagyn: ta dreeym ec ooilley jeu.”

Va gamman ayn mychione soe. “Ta soe ec dagh cretoor,” dooyrt ben va gobbraghey ayns y thie-tashtee. “She soe yn obbyr ta'n corp jannoo dy gheddyn bree ass bee. Ta soe tappee ec ushag veg.”

Ayns y shamyr jerrinagh, va cummey jeh inçhyn. “Ta inçhyn mooar ec y sheelnaue,” dooyrt Gerald. “Shen yn oyr dy vel y sheelnaue abyl lhaih, screeu as smooinaghtyn.” Va jalloo jeh shennaghys y sheelnaue er y voalley, veih ny chied deiney gys y sleih jiu.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi hie marish Ffion dys y thie-tashtee?
Hie e shenn-ayr Gerald Kinnear marish.
Cre va ayns y chied shamyr?
Va ushylagh mooar feeaih ayn.
Cre'n daah va'n clooie er yn ushag?
Va'n clooie gorrym.
Cre ta ayns killag eukaryotagh?
Ta mynoltyn ayns killag eukaryotagh.
Raad ta archaea cummal?
Ta archaea cummal ayns ushtey feer çheh.

lessons.title: Oie sheanse
lessons.summary: Marcus Fenton, a science teacher in Peel, gives an evening show for pupils: he examines ice with a thermometer, shows droplets evaporating, compares the density of oil and water, explains covalent bonds, and talks about asteroids and neutron stars; Yasmin wants to study applied science.
lessons.text:
She ynseyder sheanse ayns scoill ayns Pheeil eh Marcus Fenton. Dagh blein, t'eh jannoo oie sheanse son ny studeyryn. 'Sy vlein shoh, haink keead studeyr as paarantyn.

Hoshiaght, ghow Marcus peesh dy rio. “She stooaltane rio,” dooyrt eh. “Nish, lhig dooin y rio y scrutaghey.” Hug eh tempreilyssane ayns y rio. Va 0 er y tempreilyssane. Eisht hug eh y rio er aile beg. Lurg tammylt, va'n stooaltane çhyndaait gys ushtey, as va 10 er y tempreilyssane.

“Jeeagh er ny bineenyn er y chappan,” dooyrt Marcus. Va bineenyn beggey ushtey er y chappan. “Tra ta'n ushtey çheh, ta ny bineenyn gaalaghey. Ta gaalaghey cur yn ushtey stiagh 'syn aer.” Lurg tammylt, cha row bineen erbee er y chappan. Va ny bineenyn ooilley ersooyl.

Eisht hug eh ooill as ushtey ayns un chappan. Va'n ooill er yn ushtey. “Cre'n fa?” dooyrt eh. Dooyrt studeyr aeg, Yasmin, “Ta glooaght yn ooill ny sloo na glooaght yn ushtey.” “Kiart!” dooyrt Marcus. “Ta glooaght ny smoo ec yn ushtey, as myr shen t'eh fo'n ooill.”

Ren eh jalloo jeh ushtey er y voayrd: daa vreneen hiddragien as un vreneen ocsygien. “Ta kianglaghyn cofioosagh eddyr ny breneenyn shoh,” dooyrt eh. “Ayns kiangley cofioosagh, ta daa vreneen goaill ayrn ayns lectraneyn.”

Ec y jerrey, ren eh loayrt mychione y speyr. “She roltageagh clagh mooar ta goll mygeayrt y ghrian,” dooyrt eh. “Ta ram roltageagh 'sy speyr. As ta rollageyn naeearaneagh ayn myrgeddin. Ta rollage naeearaneagh feer veg, agh ta'n glooaght eck feer vooar: ta cappan lane jeh cho trome as slieau!”

Lurg yn oie, dooyrt Yasmin rish Marcus, “S'mie lhiam sheanse feamagh. Ta mee laccal gobbraghey ayns sheanse feamagh.” Agh, va Yasmin laccal y speyr y scrutaghey myrgeddin. “Foddee oo sheanse feamagh as y speyr y ynsaghey,” dooyrt Marcus.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr t'ec Marcus Fenton?
She ynseyder sheanse eh.
Cre hug Marcus ayns y rio?
Hug eh tempreilyssane ayns y rio.
Cre haghyr da ny bineenyn er y chappan?
Ren ny bineenyn gaalaghey.
Cre'n fa va'n ooill er yn ushtey?
Va glooaght yn ooill ny sloo na glooaght yn ushtey.
Cre ta Yasmin laccal y ynsaghey?
Ta Yasmin laccal sheanse feamagh y ynsaghey.

lessons.title: Yn oie vardaght
lessons.summary: Enid Bellamy, an old poet, reads at the annual poetry evening in Ramsey with her grandson Lorcan: he is eighth on the list and she is fifth, their poems are about three generations of the family and an obedient old dog, and the audience shows great understanding.
lessons.text:
Ta Enid Bellamy kiare feed bleeaney d'eash, as t'ee screeu bardaght neayr's v'ee aeg. Dagh blein, ta oie vardaght vleeanagh ayns Rhumsaa, as ta Enid cliaghtey frastyl ec yn oie shen. 'Sy vlein shoh, hie Lorcan, mac e mac, marish. Ta Lorcan shiaght bleeaney jeig d'eash, as t'eh screeu bardaght myrgeddin.

Va'n oie vardaght vleeanagh ayns thie-oast faggys da'n phurt. Va list er y voalley, lesh ennym dagh fer as dagh ben va lhaih bardaght. Va Enid yn queigoo ben er y list, as va Lorcan yn hoghtoo fer. “Cha nel mee laccal ve yn hoghtoo fer,” dooyrt Lorcan. “Bee ny sleih er goll thie roish yn hoghtoo fer!” “Cha bee,” dooyrt Enid.

Va three feed dooinney as ben ayns y thie-oast son frastyl ec yn oie. Ren yn chied fer lhaih bardaght mychione y keayn, as y nah ben bardaght mychione graih. Eisht haink Enid, y queigoo ben er y list.

Va bardaght Enid mychione three sheeloghe jeh'n lught-thie eck: e moir, ee hene as e mac. “Ta dagh sheeloghe ynsaghey veih'n sheeloghe roish,” lhaih ee. Va bardaght Enid meen as feayr. Va tushtey mooar ec y sleih er y vardaght eck, as va taitnys mooar oc.

Ec y jerrey, haink Lorcan. Va bardaght Lorcan mychione moddey shenn va ec y lught-thie. “V'eh biallagh dy kinjagh,” lhaih eh. “Tra dooyrt shin ‘Tar!’, haink eh. V'eh biallagh, as v'eh meen.” Ren ny sleih gearey. Va tushtey oc er y vardaght.

Lurg yn oie, dooyrt Enid, “Va oo yn hoghtoo er y list, agh she oo yn fer share!” Va taitnys mooar ec Lorcan. “Bee mee frastyl ec yn oie vardaght vleeanagh 'sy vlein noa,” dooyrt eh.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n eash t'ec Enid Bellamy?
T'ee kiare feed bleeaney d'eash.
Raad va'n oie vardaght vleeanagh?
V'ee ayns thie-oast ayns Rhumsaa.
Cre'n ynnyd va ec Enid er y list?
Va Enid yn queigoo ben er y list.
Cre mychione va bardaght Enid?
V'ee mychione three sheeloghe jeh'n lught-thie eck.
Cre mychione va bardaght Lorcan?
V'ee mychione moddey shenn biallagh.

lessons.title: Bluckaneyrys ayns Nerin
lessons.summary: Three friends, Colm Kerkin, Russell and Dafydd, travel to Ireland to see Gaelic football for the first time: a ferry and a long journey by car, a sudden brake at a crossroads, the climb up to the ground following the crowd, a pitch wider than a soccer pitch and a high standard of play.
lessons.text:
She troor caarjyn ad Colm Kerkin, Russell as Dafydd. Ta'n troor oc cloie soccer ayns Doolish, agh cha row ad rieau er vakin bluckaneyrys. Ayns Mee Averil, hie yn troor oc dys Nerin dy akin bluckaneyrys.

Va'n jurnaa liauyr. Hoshiaght, ghow ad y baatey dys Divlyn. Eisht, ghow ad carbyd, as hie ad hiar. Va'n balley lesh y vagher bluckaneyrys keead meeilley veih Divlyn. “Keead meeilley!” dooyrt Russell. “Ta'n jurnaa shoh ro liauyr.”

Ec crossag er y raad, haink cabbyl magh er y raad. Hug Colm yn glackan er dy tappee, as hass y carbyd. Va'n glackan mie, as va'n cabbyl as y carbyd slane. Ec y nah chrossag, va cowrey: “Magher bluckaneyrys, jeih meeilley.”

Va'n magher er cronk. Va ram sleih shooyl sheose y cronk. “Eiyr orrym!” dooyrt Colm. “Lhig dooin eiyrt er y sleih.” Hie ad sheose y cronk, as ren ad eiyrt er ny sleih gys y magher.

Va'n magher bluckaneyrys mooar. “T'eh ny s'lhea na magher soccer,” dooyrt Russell. “Ta, as t'eh ny s'liauyr myrgeddin,” dooyrt Dafydd. “Ta'n magher shoh ny s'lhea as ny s'liauyr.”

Ayns bluckaneyrys, ta ny cloiederyn goaill y bluckan lesh nyn laueyn as nyn gassyn. Va'n stundayrt feer ard. Va ny cloiederyn tappee as lajer. “Ta'n stundayrt ny share na'n stundayrt ain ayns Doolish!” dooyrt Russell.

Lurg y gamman, hie yn troor oc sheese y cronk. “Ta'n jurnaa er ve feeu eh,” dooyrt Colm. “Bee shin çheet reesht 'sy vlein noa.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va'n troor caarjyn?
Va Colm Kerkin, Russell as Dafydd yn troor caarjyn.
Cre cho foddey va'n magher veih Divlyn?
V'eh keead meeilley veih Divlyn.
Cre haghyr ec y chrossag?
Haink cabbyl magh, as hug Colm yn glackan er.
Quoi ren ad eiyrt er sheose y cronk?
Ren ad eiyrt er ny sleih.
Vel magher bluckaneyrys ny s'lhea na magher soccer?
Ta. T'eh ny s'lhea na magher soccer.

lessons.title: Y Flah
lessons.summary: Selina Hollis acts in a new Manx-language TV sitcom written by Vincent Pritchard: in the sitcom a foolish prince rules a colonial island and must hold an election, a liberal statesman forms a coalition, and the government's own vote goes wrong; the media like it.
lessons.text:
Ta Selina Hollis ny aghteyr. 'Sy vlein shoh, t'ee cloie ayns sitcom noa ayns Gaelg er y çhellveeish. Ta'n sitcom screeuit ec Vincent Pritchard. Ta ennym y sitcom “Y Flah”.

Ayns y sitcom, ta flah aeg reill ellan veg 'sy traa coloinagh. Ta'n flah aeg, as cha nel fys echey er veg. T'eh cliaghtey cadley ayns oik reiltyssagh, as ta ny fir reiltyssagh jannoo yn obbyr ooilley. She Selina yn ven-obbree reiltyssagh ta jannoo yn obbyr s'trome.

Ayns y chied ayrn, ta'n reiltys coloinagh gra dy vel feme er y flah reihys y chur er bun. Cha nel fys ec y flah cre ta reihys. “Cre ta vote?” t'eh gra. “Ta vote ec dagh dooinney as dagh ben,” ta Selina gra. “Ta dagh vote scanshoil.” Ta'n flah laccal vote hene, agh cha nel vote ec flah!

Ta'n reihys gaase ny smoo aitt. Ta steateyr libraalagh shenn çheet dys yn ellan. T'eh laccal cochaarjys y yannoo eddyr y partee libraalagh as partee elley. “Lesh cochaarjys, vees y pooar ain,” ta'n steateyr gra. Agh ta'n flah credjal dy vel cochaarjys ny sorçh dy vee!

Ec y jerrey, ta'n reihys çheet. Ta lettyr reihyssagh goll magh dys dagh thie, agh ta'n oik reiltyssagh er chur ennym y flah er dagh lettyr reihyssagh. Ta'n flah reiht, ga nagh row eh ayns y reihys. Ta'n steateyr libraalagh as Selina gearey.

Ta'n ym-ysseraght ayns Ellan Vannin goaill taitnys 'sy sitcom. Va naight ayns y pabyr-naight mychione y sitcom, as ren y radio loayrt rish Vincent. “Ta'n ym-ysseraght cur kiarail da Gaelg reesht,” dooyrt Vincent. “Shen yn red share.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ren y sitcom y screeu?
Ren Vincent Pritchard y sitcom y screeu.
Quoi ta reill yn ellan ayns y sitcom?
Ta flah aeg reill yn ellan.
Vel vote ec y flah?
Cha nel. Cha nel vote ec y flah.
Cre ta'n steateyr libraalagh laccal y yannoo?
T'eh laccal cochaarjys y yannoo.
Cre ren yn ym-ysseraght?
Ghow yn ym-ysseraght taitnys 'sy sitcom.

lessons.title: Y rang Gaelg
lessons.summary: Maeve Marsh teaches an evening Manx class paid for by a government grant; Quentin Ashby is confused by voiceless consonants, Maeve corrects him patiently, explains that the best way is real conversation, and he promises to come for a long while.
lessons.text:
Ta Maeve Marsh ynsaghey Gaelg ayns Doolish. Dagh Jeheiney, ta rang oie eck. Ta'n reiltys cur argid coonee son y rang. Gyn yn argid coonee, cha beagh y rang ayn. 'Sy vlein shoh, ta kiare dooiney jeig 'sy rang. Ta dagh dooiney ayns y rang laccal Gaelg y loayrt.

She Quentin Ashby fer jeh ny studeyryn. T'eh feer arryltagh, agh ta boirey er mychione sheean ny focklyn. Laa dy row, dooyrt Maeve, “Jiu, ta shin ynsaghey corocklyn neuchronnaneagh.”

“Cre ta neuchronnaneagh?” dooyrt Quentin. Va boirey er.

“Ta'n scoarnagh craa tra ta shin gra corockle cadjin,” dooyrt Maeve. “Cha nel y scoarnagh craa tra ta shin gra corockle neuchronnaneagh. Cur dty laue er dty scoarnagh, as abbyr ‘pabyr’ as eisht ‘bainney’.” Ren Quentin shen. “Ta, ta mee ennaghtyn eh!” dooyrt eh. Cha row boirey er nish.

Eisht, lhaih Quentin skeeal beg. Va ram focklyn ayn nagh row kiart, as ren Maeve kiartaghey er ny focklyn shen dy meen. “Cha nel kiartaghey drogh red,” dooyrt ee. “She kiartaghey yn aght dy ynsaghey.”

“Cre'n mod share dy ynsaghey Gaelg?” dooyrt Quentin.

“Ta ram mod ayn,” dooyrt Maeve. “Lioaryn, radio, arraneyn as lhied. Agh she yn mod share, loayrt rish sleih rieughagh. Loayr rish sleih rieughagh ayns ynnydyn rieughagh: ayns y margey, ayns y thie-oast as lhied.” Va lhied ny focklyn shen feer vie da Quentin.

Ec jerrey yn rang, dooyrt Quentin, “Ta mee giall dhyt dy jig mee dagh Jeheiney.” “Giall?” dooyrt Maeve. “Ta mee giall,” dooyrt eh. “Bee mee ayns shoh son shayll liauyr.”

As haink eh. Lurg shayll dy hoght meeaghyn, v'eh loayrt Gaelg rish sleih rieughagh 'sy thie-oast.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta cur argid son y rang?
Ta'n reiltys cur argid coonee son y rang.
Cre wheesh dooiney t'ayns y rang?
Ta kiare dooiney jeig 'sy rang.
Cre ren boirey er Quentin?
Ren corocklyn neuchronnaneagh boirey er.
Cre'n mod share dy ynsaghey Gaelg, rere Maeve?
She loayrt rish sleih rieughagh yn mod share.
Cre ren Quentin giall?
Ren eh giall dy jig eh dagh Jeheiney.

lessons.title: Feaill y vee ayns Pheeil
lessons.summary: Philippa Gale and her son Tobias go to a food festival in Peel: vegetables from a farm whose livestock graze on pasture, hot salmon, a stall from Turkey with sweet and bitter oranges, and a talk about nature and the temperate climate.
lessons.text:
Dagh blein, ta feaill vee ayns Pheeil. 'Sy vlein shoh, hie Philippa Gale as e mac Tobias dys y feaill. Ta Tobias nuy bleeaney d'eash.

Ec y chied boayrd, va eirinagh creck glassrey. Va glassrey jiarg, glassrey glass as glassrey buigh er y voayrd. “Ta'n glassrey shoh veih'n thalloo ain,” dooyrt yn eirinagh. “Ta sthock ain myrgeddin: kirree as cabbil. Ta'n sthock geddyn bee er thalloo fassee glass faggys da'n cheayn.” “Ta thalloo fassee mie ayns Ellan Vannin,” dooyrt Philippa.

Ec y nah boayrd, va braddan. Va'n braddan çheh veih'n aile. Ghow Tobias peesh veg. “T'eh blasstal!” dooyrt eh. “Braddan blasstal!” “Ta braddan cummal 'sy cheayn,” dooyrt y dooinney ec y voayrd, “agh t'eh goll seose ny h-awinyn.”

Ec y trass boayrd, va ben veih'n Turkee. Va oranjeyn er y voayrd eck, as bee veih'n Turkee. “Ta oranjeyn mooarey aase ayns y Turkee,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n ghrian çheh ayns y Turkee.” Va oranjeyn millish ayn, as va oranjeyn sharroo ayn. Ghow Tobias oranje sharroo, as ren e eddin çhyndaa. “T'eh sharroo!” dooyrt eh. “Ta,” dooyrt y ven. “Agh ta oranje sharroo blasstal ayns bee millish.”

Ec jerrey y laa, va fer-ynsee veih'n ollooscoill loayrt mychione najoor. “Ta'n emshir ayns Ellan Vannin tempreilagh,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel ee ro çheh, as cha nel ee ro feayr. Ayns emshir tempreilagh, ta glassrey aase dy mie, as ta'n najoor bishagh.” “Ta oranjeyn feme emshir ny s'çheh na emshir tempreilagh,” dooyrt Tobias. “Kiart,” dooyrt y fer-ynsee. “Shen yn oyr dy vel ad çheet veih'n Turkee.”

Chionnee Philippa glassrey, braddan as oranjeyn son y thie.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va'n eirinagh creck?
Va'n eirinagh creck glassrey.
Raad ta'n sthock geddyn bee?
Ta'n sthock geddyn bee er thalloo fassee faggys da'n cheayn.
Cre ghow Tobias ec y nah boayrd?
Ghow eh peesh veg dy vraddan.
Raad va'n ven veih?
Va'n ven veih'n Turkee.
Cre'n sorçh dy emshir t'ayns Ellan Vannin?
Ta emshir tempreilagh ayns Ellan Vannin.

lessons.title: Y tobbyr casherick
lessons.summary: On a heritage walk one morning, guide Rhiannon Dobbs leads a group with blind visitor Fraser Teague along a stream to a holy well that a priest blessed, past a dangerous path and a cave where people took refuge when the Vikings raided in that period.
lessons.text:
Dagh moghrey Jeheiney, ta Rhiannon Dobbs goll er shooyl marish possan dy leih dys shenn tobbyr casherick faggys da Rhumsaa. Va'n moghrey shoh feayr as fliugh.

Va dooinney doal 'sy phossan, Fraser Teague. Ta Fraser doal neayr's v'eh paitçhey. “Cha nel mee fakin red erbee,” dooyrt eh, “agh ta mee clashtyn as ennaghtyn ram.” Ghow Rhiannon e laue.

Hie ad er cassan liorish strooan. Va'n strooan beg as glen. “Cur geill da'n strooan,” dooyrt Rhiannon. “T'eh roie sheese dys y keayn.” “Ta'n strooan shoh aalin,” dooyrt Fraser.

Eisht va'n cassan gaueagh. Va claghyn fliugh er y chassan, as va'n strooan dowin. “Ta'n cassan shoh gaueagh,” dooyrt Rhiannon. Hug Fraser e laue er boalley.

Ec y tobbyr, ghow Rhiannon lioar veg ass e poagey. Lhaih ee: “Va'n tobbyr shoh bannit ec saggyrt ayns earish ny Lochlynee. Va'n saggyrt bannee yn ushtey, as v'eh bannee ny sleih ayns y balley.” Hug Fraser e laue 'sy tobbyr. “T'eh feayr!” dooyrt eh.

Faggys da'n tobbyr va ooig. “Ayns earish ny Lochlynee,” dooyrt Rhiannon, “haink ny Lochlynee dy ruegey yn ellan. Tra va ny Lochlynee ruegey, hie ny sleih stiagh 'syn ooig. Va'n ooig ny kemmyrk daue. Cha row ny Lochlynee abyl yn ooig y gheddyn.” Hie ad stiagh 'syn ooig. Va'n ooig dorraghey as feayr. “Ta mee ennaghtyn dy vel shoh kemmyrk,” dooyrt Fraser.

Haink ad reesht dys y balley ec jerrey y voghree. Hug Fraser clagh veg veih'n strooan ayns e phoagey.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta Fraser Teague?
She dooinney doal eh.
Cre'n fa va'n cassan gaueagh?
Va claghyn fliugh er y chassan, as va'n strooan dowin.
Quoi va bannee yn ushtey?
Va saggyrt bannee yn ushtey.
Cre'n fa hie ny sleih stiagh 'syn ooig?
Hie ad stiagh 'syn ooig tra va ny Lochlynee ruegey yn ellan.
Cre hug Fraser ayns e phoagey?
Hug eh clagh veg veih'n strooan ayns e phoagey.

lessons.title: Lhong ny Lochlynee
lessons.summary: Engineer Morwenna Hurst and sailor Bridget Ormsby repair a replica Viking ship before the festival in Peel: a crack in the hull, new ropes, the ship moved to the harbour, the flag raised higher, and the festival helping the island's economy.
lessons.text:
She jeshaghteyr ee Morwenna Hurst. T'ee gobbraghey ayns Pheeil. Dagh blein, ta feaill ny Lochlynee ayns Pheeil, as ta lhong noa çheet dys y phurt. She lhong fuygh ee, jeant myr shenn lhongyn ny Lochlynee.

'Sy vlein shoh, va boirey ayn. Va scoltey ayns y lhong. Haink Bridget Ormsby dys Morwenna. She shiaulteyr ee Bridget, as she ish captan y lhong. “Ta scoltey ayns y lhong,” dooyrt y shiaulteyr. “Vel oo abyl y scoltey y chur kiart?”

Ren y jeshaghteyr y scoltey y scrutaghey. “She scoltey beg eh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta mee abyl y scoltey y chur kiart ayns three laa.” Ren y jeshaghteyr fuygh noa y chur ayns y scoltey.

Eisht, ren y shiaulteyr jeeaghyn er ny strengyn. Va ny strengyn shenn. “Ta feme ain er strengyn noa,” dooyrt ee. Chionnee ad strengyn noa ayns Doolish, as ren y shiaulteyr ny strengyn noa y chiangley er y lhong.

Lurg shen, ren ad y lhong y astreeaghey veih'n thie-lhong dys y phurt. Ren jees dooinney as carbyd mooar y lhong y astreeaghey. Va'n astreeaghey trome, agh lurg oor, va'n lhong 'sy phurt.

Ec y jerrey, ren ad y brattagh y ardjaghey. Ren y shiaulteyr y brattagh y ardjaghey lesh ny strengyn noa. “Ny s'ardjey!” dooyrt y jeshaghteyr. Hie'n brattagh ny s'ardjey as ny s'ardjey, derrey v'eh ard erskyn y lhong.

Haink ram sleih dys y feaill. Ta'n feaill mie son y farrys. Ta ny sleih ceau argid ayns ny shappyn as ayns ny thieyn-oast. “Ta'n lhong mie son y farrys ayns Pheeil,” dooyrt Bridget. “As ta'n farrys mie son y jeshaghteyr!” dooyrt Morwenna, as ren ad gearey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr t'ec Morwenna Hurst?
She jeshaghteyr ee.
Cre va ayns y lhong?
Va scoltey ayns y lhong.
Cre'n fa va feme oc er strengyn noa?
Va ny strengyn shenn.
Cre ren ad ec y jerrey?
Ren ad y brattagh y ardjaghey.
Cre'n fa ta'n feaill mie son y farrys?
Ta ny sleih ceau argid ayns ny shappyn.
